name: Ten Commandments
hook: Moses, Mount Sinai and the two Cecil B. DeMille epics that fixed them on film.

facts.label: Mount Sinai
facts.statement: Moses receives the commandments on Mount Sinai, also called Mount Horeb; Jabal Musa, 7,497 feet high, is traditionally identified as the peak.

facts.label: Exodus
facts.statement: The commandments first appear in the Book of Exodus, and their other name, the Decalogue, comes from Greek for 'ten words.'

facts.label: the tablets
facts.statement: Moses breaks the first set of tablets when he sees the golden calf; the second set is kept in the Ark of the Covenant.

facts.label: the sabbath
facts.statement: The fourth commandment says 'Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy'; another tells children to honor their father and mother.

facts.label: Cecil B. DeMille
facts.statement: DeMille directed both the 1923 silent epic and the 1956 remake, and The Ten Commandments was the last film he directed.

facts.label: Charlton Heston
facts.statement: Charlton Heston plays Moses in the 1956 film and also supplies God's slowed-down burning-bush voice.

facts.label: the 1956 cast
facts.statement: Edward G. Robinson plays the sneering Dathan, Yvonne De Carlo plays Moses' wife, and John Carradine plays Aaron in the 1956 film.
